item.title: The Climates of Other Worlds: A Review of the Emerging Field of Exoplanet Climatology
Comparative Analysis of the Model for Exoplanet Atmosphere Outflow
Accelerating Radiative Transfer for Planetary Atmospheres by Orders of Magnitude with a Transformer-Based Machine Learning Model

notes: Let's begin with how gravity holds gas around a planet, just like the air on Mars in that book. This layer of vapor is kept close by the object's own pull.
Building on that, we see other worlds also wrap themselves in these gaseous skins. Giant planets and moons far away have their own unique envelopes too.
From there, scientists look for specific gases to guess if life exists elsewhere. Since data is scarce, they often use what we know about Earth and our Solar System as a guide.
With that in hand, we must understand how temperature and weather on other planets change over time. Many factors influence these climates, making them hard to predict accurately.
Stepping up a level, models now track how atmospheres escape into space completely. These complex simulations help us see how entire planetary systems evolve and fade away.
Finally, new computer tricks speed up the math needed to study heat moving through air. This lets us run detailed tests without waiting too long for answers.
